neighbours.label: verb or preposition right before its object refers back to something already mentioned (talk about [it], see [it], stop [it])
fire: The rumour upset her so much that she refused to talk about it at dinner.
Everyone said the new film was great, so we drove downtown to see it.
The leak kept getting worse and nobody knew how to stop it before morning.
He found the old letter in a drawer and decided to read it again.
My grandmother baked the cake herself, and we could hardly wait to taste it.
The report was finished on Friday, and the editor promised to check it soon.
When the dog found the ball, it ran off and refused to give it back.
The question puzzled the class, and the teacher tried hard to answer it.
quiet: The rumour upset her so much that she refused to come down for dinner.
Everyone said the weather was great, so we drove downtown in the afternoon.
The leak kept getting worse and nobody knew what was happening in the basement.
He found the old letter in a drawer and sat quietly for a while.
My grandmother baked all morning, and we could hardly wait for lunch.
The report was finished on Friday, and the editor went home early.
When the dog found the ball, it ran off across the garden happily.
The question puzzled the class, and the teacher paused for a long moment.

notes: Card flags broad (2% of tokens). Top examples peak on ' about', ' see', ' stop', ' the' just before 'it'/'the story'.
